programs.name: PAVE
programs.full: Program Against Abuse, Violence and Exploitation
programs.what: Protective services for women and children: case management for victims of violence, psychosocial support, referrals and community campaigns such as Stop Karahasan.
programs.impact: More survivors are reached and more barangays are speaking up. Faster response means safer homes across Romblon's municipalities.

programs.name: HERO
programs.full: Helping Every Solo Parent with Resources and Opportunities
programs.what: Registers solo parents, issues Solo Parent IDs and connects them to the benefits and discounts of the Expanded Solo Parents Welfare Act.
programs.impact: Single mothers and fathers gain recognition, discounts and a path to livelihood, easing the load on one-income households.

programs.name: Golden Life
programs.what: Assistance, benefits and recognition for older Romblomanons, from welfare support to honoring the province's elders.
programs.impact: Nearly twice as many seniors were served, bringing dignity and support to older persons on islands far from the capital.

programs.name: AICS
programs.full: Assistance to Individuals in Crisis Situations
programs.what: The province's frontline for emergencies: medical, burial, transportation, food and educational assistance for families in sudden crisis.
programs.impact: When a family faces a hospital bill or a funeral they cannot afford, AICS is often the difference between recovery and ruin.

programs.name: RHAP
programs.what: Helps residents with hospital bills, medicines and referrals so that no family has to choose between health and survival.
programs.impact: The largest program by reach. Nine thousand Romblomanons received health assistance that would otherwise have pushed them into debt.

programs.name: Youth / SDEC
programs.full: Youth Development and Special Drug Education Center
programs.what: Prevention education, counseling and development activities that guide young people away from drugs and toward productive lives.
programs.impact: Reach declined this year. The office treats this as a signal to strengthen staffing and school and barangay outreach in 2027.

programs.name: Child Development Center
programs.what: Supports the province's Child Development Centers and the workers who run them, where early childhood learning begins.
programs.impact: A steady foundation for Romblon's youngest learners, with 306 centers and workers supported provincewide.

programs.name: CNSP
programs.full: Children in Need of Special Protection
programs.what: Case management, placement and protective care for children who are abandoned, neglected, abused or exploited.
programs.impact: More vulnerable children are being found and protected. Each case is a child removed from harm and placed on a path to healing.

programs.name: CICL
programs.full: Children in Conflict with the Law
programs.what: Diversion, rehabilitation and reintegration for children in conflict with the law under the Juvenile Justice and Welfare Act, anchored at Bahay Pag-asa.
programs.impact: Thirteen children were given intervention and a second chance instead of detention.

challenges.title: Workforce Capacity, Staffing and Retention
concerns: Reliance on COS / JO personnel and high turnover
Limited case managers, technical support and supervisors
challenges.impact: Overlapping functions, heavy caseloads, limited supervision and continuity, and delays in implementation, monitoring and reporting.
challenges.response: Fill critical plantilla positions; assign dedicated case managers and technical support; strengthen retention and workload allocation.

challenges.title: Facility Completion and Operational Readiness
concerns: Leaking roofs, damaged tiles and inadequate water storage
Unfinished gates and other readiness requirements
challenges.impact: Delayed center operations, safety concerns and difficulty meeting center-based service targets.
challenges.response: Complete and inspect facilities; address safety and structural deficiencies; provide essential utilities, equipment and readiness standards.

challenges.title: Funding Adequacy and Timely Assistance
concerns: Limited AICS and hospital assistance funds
Need for supplemental appropriations or realignment
challenges.impact: Pending client requests, unpaid hospital billings and delays in assistance to individuals and families in crisis.
challenges.response: Review funding needs and utilization; prioritize urgent cases; pursue timely augmentation or realignment.

scenes.title: Serbisyong May Puso
scenes.narration: Serbisyong May Puso. From January to October 2026, the Provincial Social Welfare and Development Office of Romblon reached 22,513 clients across the province. Behind every one of these numbers is a family, a child, or an elder whose life was touched. This is our story.

scenes.title: Our Mandate
scenes.narration: The PSWDO promotes social protection, upholds human dignity, and enhances the well-being of disadvantaged individuals, families, and communities. Six major final outputs guide this work: approving policies and plans, implementing social protection programs, running centers and institutions, delivering special operations, providing technical assistance, and ensuring compliance with provincial rules.

scenes.title: The People Behind the Service
scenes.narration: Who delivers these services? 92 personnel, including 12 licensed social workers, spread across every program. Twenty staff serve under Golden Life, nineteen at Bahay Pag-asa, and sixteen in Productivity Skills and Capability Building. Yet only nine positions are permanent. Most of this work rests on contractual and job-order personnel.

scenes.title: Accomplishments at a Glance
scenes.narration: In ten months, 7 programs, 16 projects, and more than 98 activities reached 22,513 clients. Compared with 2025, nearly every program grew, and some more than doubled. Let's look at each one.

scenes.title: PAVE
scenes.narration: PAVE, the Program Against Abuse, Violence and Exploitation, protects women and children from violence through case management, psychosocial support, and community campaigns like Stop Karahasan. Clients served jumped from 1,308 to 3,409, a 160 percent increase. More survivors are being reached, and more communities are speaking up.

scenes.title: HERO
scenes.narration: HERO, Helping Every Solo Parent with Resources and Opportunities, registers solo parents, issues their IDs, and connects them to the benefits of the Expanded Solo Parents Welfare Act. 903 solo parents were served this year, up 22 percent from 737.

scenes.title: Golden Life
scenes.narration: Golden Life is our program for senior citizens, delivering assistance, benefits, and recognition to older Romblomanons. Reach nearly doubled, from 1,788 to 3,374 seniors, an 88 percent increase.

scenes.title: AICS
scenes.narration: AICS, Assistance to Individuals in Crisis Situations, is the province's frontline for emergencies: medical, burial, transportation, food, and educational assistance. 3,950 individuals and families received help, 22 percent more than last year.

scenes.title: RHAP
scenes.narration: The Romblon Health Access Program is our largest program by reach. It helps residents with hospital bills, medicines, and referrals, so that no family has to choose between health and survival. 9,329 clients were assisted, up 48 percent from 6,293.

scenes.title: Youth / SDEC
scenes.narration: Our Youth and Special Drug Education Center programs guide young people through prevention education, counseling, and development activities. Reach declined 17.7 percent, from 1,425 to 1,173. We treat this honestly: it signals where staffing and outreach must be strengthened in 2027.

scenes.title: Child Development Centers
scenes.narration: Child Development Centers are where early learning begins. 306 centers and workers were supported this year, the same as last year, a steady foundation for Romblon's youngest learners.

scenes.title: CNSP
scenes.narration: Children in Need of Special Protection are those who are abandoned, neglected, or abused. 56 children were placed under protective case management this year, up from 21. That is a 167 percent increase, meaning more vulnerable children are being found and protected.

scenes.title: CICL
scenes.narration: For Children in Conflict with the Law, the office provides diversion, rehabilitation, and reintegration under the Juvenile Justice and Welfare Act. 13 children were served, compared with 9 last year, each given a second chance instead of a sentence.

scenes.title: Centers, Accreditation and Partners
scenes.narration: Beyond direct services, the office strengthened the system itself. 76 Child Development Centers were assessed and endorsed, and 78 were accredited in 2026, bringing the province to 209 accredited centers out of 306. Bahay Pag-asa and the Productivity Skills and Capability Building center continued operating, with partners like the Ruel Foundation and Romblon State University.

scenes.title: Budget Utilization
scenes.narration: Resources were put to work. Of 44.78 million pesos across three key funds, 33.76 million was utilized. The one percent Local Council for the Protection of Children fund led at 85 percent, followed by the Senior Citizen and PWD fund at 80 percent, and the Gender and Development fund at 67 percent.

scenes.title: Issues, Gaps and Challenges
scenes.narration: Progress comes with challenges, grouped into three gaps. First, workforce capacity: only 9 of 67 plantilla positions are filled. Second, facility readiness: leaking roofs, damaged tiles, and unfinished works delay center operations. Third, funding adequacy: limited AICS and hospital assistance funds leave client requests pending. Each gap has a priority response.

scenes.title: 2027 Targets and Priorities
scenes.narration: For 2027, the priorities are clear. Fully operate the Bahay Pag-asa Youth Center. Operationalize the Crisis Center for Women and Children. Open the Haven for the Elderly. Fill critical vacant plantilla positions. And build a PSWDO Information System, so that every case is tracked and no client is left behind.

scenes.title: What It Means for Romblon
scenes.narration: What does this mean for Romblon? Across 17 municipalities and 3 major islands, roughly one in every thirteen Romblomanons was reached by a PSWDO service this year. A survivor finds safety. A solo parent finds support. A senior is honored. A patient gets treatment. A child in trouble gets a second chance. That is social protection with heart.

scenes.title: Thank You
scenes.narration: Provincial Social Welfare and Development Office. Province of Romblon. Serbisyong May Puso. Thank you.
